description: Protactinium is a dense, radioactive, silvery-gray actinide metal with atomic number 91 and symbol Pa. It readily reacts with oxygen, water vapor, and inorganic acids, and forms various chemical compounds where it is usually present in the oxidation state +5, though it can also assume +4, +3, or +2 states. It is one of the rarest and most expensive naturally occurring elements, with concentrations in the Earth's crust typically a few parts per trillion, but reaching up to a few parts per million in some uraninite ore deposits.
uses: Because of its scarcity, high radioactivity, and high toxicity, there are currently no uses for protactinium outside scientific research. In ocean science, analysis of the relative concentrations of various uranium, thorium, and protactinium isotopes in water and minerals is used in radiometric dating of sediments up to 175,000 years old and in modeling of various geological processes. Protactinium-233 is produced as an intermediate product in thorium-based nuclear reactors for the production of the fissile uranium-233.
characteristics: Protactinium is an actinide metal that is highly radioactive and toxic. It has naturally occurring isotopes 231Pa and 234Pa, with 231Pa being nearly all natural protactinium and having a half-life of 32,760 years as an alpha emitter. Thirty radioisotopes of protactinium have been discovered, ranging from 210Pa to 239Pa, with most having half-lives shorter than 1.6 days.
